decisions.topic: An ignored test is a defect signal
decisions.decision: No. Ignore status records execution cost or data availability. Treat it as an evidence gap only where a completed claim appears to rely on it, and as test robustness risk where missing inputs can produce a successful partial run.
decisions.evidence: Inspected bodies and ledger test lists; several related deterministic tests exist. No current product behavior failure was established.

decisions.decision: The test header expressly names-and-skips absent witnesses, so that behavior is documented policy rather than an automatic defect. Optional-root hardening can be narrower: skip only the absent repository root for each witness (doc/corpora/pdfbox, doc/corpora/format-corpus, doc/pdf.js), and report a missing/unreadable declared witness under a present root with its path. Parent wave-76 run passed all 3 present witnesses; negative-control proposal remains unexecuted.
decisions.recommended_change: If adopting the optional-root/partial-root distinction, use per-witness repository roots so independently optional corpora remain independent. Preserve #[ignore]. This improves evidence integrity, not PDF behavior.

decisions.decision: These supplemental runs were executed by the parent in wave 76: syntax 963 opened documents / 112562 object comparisons / 11 identical refusals; transform 3 fixtures x 3 targets x 65536 codes; accessibility 1020 documents with tracked-974 ratchet. Results add broad evidence, but are not proof that every input opens or an exhaustive corpus survey.

No such ignored corpus gate was found in that crate's test directory; its tree tests are deterministic. The related ignored source-data census is in viewer-core and should not be mislabeled as an adapter test.
